q: In a 100 m race, A can give B 10 m and C 28 m. In the same race B can give C:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & A:B = 100:90 \\ & A:C = 100:72 \\ & B:C = {B \over A} \times {A \over C} = {{90} \over {100}} \times {{100} \over {72}} = {{90} \over {72}} \end{aligned}$$ When B runs 90 m, C runs 72 m. When B runs 100m, C run $$\left( {{{72} \over {90}} \times 100} \right)m = 80\,m$$ ∴ B can give C 20 m

q: A and B take part in 100 m race. A runs at 5 kmph. A gives B a start of 8 m and still beats him by 8 seconds. The speed of B is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{A's}}{\kern 1pt} {\kern 1pt} {\text{speed}} = \left( {5 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right){\text{m/sec}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{25}}{{18}}{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Time}}{\kern 1pt} {\kern 1pt} {\text{taken}}{\kern 1pt} {\kern 1pt} {\text{by}}{\kern 1pt} {\kern 1pt} {\text{A}}{\kern 1pt} {\kern 1pt} {\text{to}}{\kern 1pt} {\kern 1pt} {\text{cover 100 m}} \\ & = \left( {100 \times \frac{{18}}{{25}}} \right)\sec \\ & = 72\sec \\ & \therefore {\text{Time}}{\kern 1pt} {\kern 1pt} {\text{taken}}{\kern 1pt} {\kern 1pt} {\text{by}}{\kern 1pt} {\kern 1pt} {\text{B}}{\kern 1pt} {\kern 1pt} {\text{to}}{\kern 1pt} {\kern 1pt} {\text{cover 92 m}} \\ & = \left( {72 + 8} \right) = 80\sec \\ & \therefore {\text{B's}}{\kern 1pt} {\kern 1pt} {\text{speed}} = \left( {\frac{{92}}{{80}} \times \frac{{18}}{5}} \right){\text{kmph}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 4.14{\text{ kmph}} \end{aligned}$$

q: In a 500 m race, the ratio of the speeds of two contestants A and B is 3 : 4. A has a start of 140 m. Then, A wins by:
s: To reach the winning post A will have to cover a distance of (500 - 140)m, i.e., 360 m. While A covers 3 m, B covers 4 m. While A covers 360 m, B covers $$\left( {\frac{4}{3} \times 360} \right)$$ m = 480 m. Thus, when A reaches the winning post, B covers 480 m and therefore remains 20 m behind. ∴ A wins by 20 m.

q: In a 100 m race, A beats B by 10 m and C by 13 m. In a race of 180 m, B will beat C by:
At a game of billiards, A can give B 15 points in 60 and A can give C to 20 points in 60. How many points can B give C in a game of 90?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & A:B = 60:45 \\ & A:C = 60:40 \\ & \therefore \frac{B}{C} = {\frac{B}{A} \times \frac{A}{C}} = {\frac{{45}}{{60}} \times \frac{{60}}{{40}}} \\ & = \frac{{45}}{{40}} = \frac{{90}}{{80}} = 90:80 \\ & \therefore {\text{B}}\,{\text{can}}\,{\text{give}}\,{\text{C}}\,{\text{10}}\,{\text{points}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{a}} \,{\text{game}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{90}} \end{aligned}$$

q: In a race of 200 m, A can beat B by 31 m and C by 18 m. In a race of 350 m, C will beat B by:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & A:B = 200:169 \\ & A:C = 200:182 \\ & \frac{C}{B} = {\frac{C}{A} \times \frac{A}{B}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = {\frac{{182}}{{200}} \times \frac{{200}}{{169}}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 182:169 \end{aligned}$$ When C covers 182 m, B covers 169 m When C covers 350 m, B covers $$\left( {\frac{{169}}{{182}} \times 350} \right){\text{m}} = 325{\text{m}}$$ ∴ C beats B by (350 - 325) m = 25 m

q: In 100 m race, A covers the distance in 36 seconds and B in 45 seconds. In this race A beats B by:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Distance covered by B in 9 sec}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{100}}{{45}} \times 9} \right){\text{m}} \\ & = 20\,{\text{m}} \\ & \therefore {\text{A beats B by 20 metres}} \end{aligned}$$

q: In a game of 100 points, A can give B 20 points and C 28 points. Then, B can give C:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & A:B = 100:80 \\ & A:C = 100:72 \\ & \therefore \frac{B}{C} = {\frac{B}{A} \times \frac{A}{C}} = {\frac{{80}}{{100}} \times \frac{{100}}{{72}}} \\ & = \frac{{10}}{9} = \frac{{100}}{{90}} = 100:90 \\ & \therefore {\text{B}}\,{\text{can}}\,{\text{give}}\,{\text{C}}\,{\text{10}}\,{\text{points}} \end{aligned}$$

q: In a 200 metres race A beats B by 35 m or 7 seconds. A's time over the course is:
s: B runs 35m in 7sec ∴ B covers 200m in $${\frac{7}{{35}} \times 200} = 40\sec$$ B's time over the course = 40 sec ∴ A's time over the course (40 - 7) sec = 33 sec

q: A can run 22.5 m while B runs 25 m. In a kilometre race B beats A by:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{When}}\,{\text{B}}\,\,{\text{runs}}\,{\text{25m,}}\,{\text{A}}\,{\text{runs}}\,\frac{{45}}{2}m \\ & {\text{When}}\,{\text{B}}\,\,{\text{runs}}\,{\text{1000m,}}\,{\text{A}}\,{\text{runs}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{45}}{2} \times \frac{1}{{25}} \times 1000} \right)m \\ & = 900 \,m \\ & \therefore {\text{B}}\,{\text{beats}}\,{\text{A}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{100 m}} \end{aligned}$$

q: In a 300 m race A beats B by 22.5 m or 6 seconds. B's time over the course is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{B runs}}\frac{{45}}{2}{\text{m in 6 sec}} \\ & \therefore {\text{B covers 300m in}} \\ & = \left( {6 \times \frac{2}{{45}} \times 300} \right)\sec \\ & = 80\,{\text{sec}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A runs $$1\frac{2}{3}$$ times as fast as B. If A gives B a start of 80 m, how far must the winning post be so that A and B might reach it at the same time?
s: Ratio of speeds of A and B $$= \frac{5}{3}:1 = 5:3$$ Thus, in race of 5m, A gains 2m over B 2m are gained by A in a race of 5m 80m will be gained by A in a race of $$\left( {\frac{5}{2} \times 80} \right){\text{m}} = 200{\text{ m}}$$ ∴ Winning post is 200 m away from the starting point

q: In a 100 m race, A can beat B by 25 m and B can beat C by 4 m. In the same race, A can beat C by:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & A:B = 100:75 \\ & B:C = 100:96 \\ & \therefore A:C = {\frac{A}{B} \times \frac{B}{C}} \\ & = {\frac{{100}}{{75}} \times \frac{{100}}{{96}}} \\ & = \frac{{100}}{{72}} \\ & 100:72 \\ & \therefore A\,\text{beats}\,C\,by \\ & = \left( {100 - 72} \right)m \\ & = 28\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: In a race of 200 m, B can give a start of 10 m to A and C can give a start of 20 m to B. The start that C can give to A in the same race is ?
s: B : A = 200 : 190 C : B = 200 : 180 $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{C}{A} \\ & = {\frac{C}{B} \times \frac{B}{A}} \\ & = {\frac{{200}}{{180}} \times \frac{{200}}{{190}}} \\ & = \frac{{200}}{{171}} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ C can give to A, a start of (200 - 171) m = 29 m

q: In a kilometre race, A beats B by 30 seconds and B beats C by 15 seconds. If A beats C by 180 m, the time taken by A to run 1 kilometre, is ?
s: In a km race, suppose A takes t sec, Then, B takes (t + 30) sec, and C takes (t + 45) sec 180 m is covered by C in 45 sec ∴ 1000 m is covered by C in = $$\left( {\frac{{45}}{{180}} \times 1000} \right)$$ sec = 250 sec ∴ A covers 1000 m in = (250 - 45) sec = 205 sec

q: A team played 40 games in a season and won in 24 of them. What percent of games played did the team win ?
s: Number of games played = 40 Number of won games = 24 Percentage of games played = $$\left( {\frac{{24}}{{40}} \times 100} \right)$$ = 60%

q: In a kilometre race, A, B and C are three participants. A can give B start of 50 m and C a start of 69 m. The start which B can allow C, is -
s: A : B : C = 1000 : (1000 - 50) : (1000 - 69) = 1000 : 950 : 931 In a 950 m race, B can give C a start of (950 - 931) m = 19 m In a 1000 m race, B can give C a start of = $$\left( {\frac{{19}}{{950}} \times 1000} \right)$$ = 20 m

q: A and B take part in a 100 metres race. A runs at 5 km an hour. A gives B a start of 8 metres and still beats him by 8 seconds. The speed of B is ?
s: A's speed = 5 km/hr = $$\left( {5 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right)$$ m/sec = $$\frac{25}{18}$$ m/sec Time taken by A to cover 100 metres = $$\left( {100 \times \frac{{18}}{{25}}} \right)$$ = 72 sec Time taken by B to cover 92 metres = (72 + 8) sec = 80 sec B's speed $$\frac{92}{80}$$ m/sec = $$\left( {\frac{{92}}{{80}} \times \frac{{18}}{5}} \right)$$ km/hr = $$\frac{414}{100}$$ km/hr = 4.14 km/hr

q: In a 400 m race, A gives B a start of 5 seconds and beats him by 15 m. In another race of 400 m, A beats B by $$7\frac{1}{7}$$ seconds. Their respective speed are -
s: Suppose A covers 400 m in t seconds Then, B covers 385 m in (t + 5) seconds $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ B covers 400 m in}} \\ & = \left\{ {\frac{{\left( {t + 5} \right)}}{{385}} \times 400} \right\}{\text{ sec}} \\ & = \frac{{80\left( {t + 5} \right)}}{{77}}{\text{ sec}} \\ & {\text{Also, B covers 400 m in}} \\ & = \left( {t + 7\frac{1}{7}} \right){\text{ sec}} \\ & = \frac{{\left( {7t + 50} \right)}}{7}{\text{ sec}} \\ & \therefore \frac{{80\left( {t + 5} \right)}}{{77}} = \frac{{7t + 50}}{7} \\ & \Rightarrow 80\left( {t + 5} \right) = 11\left( {7t + 50} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {80t - 77t} \right) = \left( {550 - 400} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow 3t = 150 \\ & \Rightarrow t = 50 \\ & \therefore {\text{ A's speed}} \\ & = \frac{{400}}{{50}}\,m/\sec \\ & = 8\,m/\sec \\ & \therefore {\text{B's speed}} \\ & = \frac{{385}}{{55}}\,m/\sec \\ & = 7\,m/\sec \end{aligned}$$

q: In a kilometre race, A beats B by 100 m and B beats C by 150 m. In the same race, by how many metres does A beat C ?
A and B can cover a 200 m race in 22 seconds and 25 seconds respectively. When Av finished the race, then B is at what distance from the finishing line ?
s: Distance covered by B in 25 sec = 200 m Distance covered by B in 22 sec =$$\left( {\frac{{200}}{{25}} \times 22} \right)$$ m = 176 m ∴ B was at a distance of (200 - 176) m = 24 m from the finishing line.

q: In a 1000 m race, A can beat B by 100 m. In a race of 400 m, B can beat C by 40 m. By how many metres will A beat C in a race of 500 m ?
In a 200 m race, A beats B by 35 m or 7 seconds. A's time over the course is-
s: B covers 35 m in 7 seconds. B covers 200 m in = $$\left( {\frac{7}{{35}} \times 200} \right)$$ sec = 40 sec Time taken by A = (40 - 7) sec = 33 sec

q: In a 800 metre race, A defeated B by 15 seconds. If A's speed was 8 km/hr, the speed of B was -
s: A's speed = 8 km/hr = $$\left( {8 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right)$$ m/sec = $$\frac{20}{9}$$ m/sec Time taken by A to cover 800 m = $$\left( {800 \times \frac{9}{{20}}} \right)$$ sec = 360 sec Time taken by B to cover 800 m = (360 + 15) sec = 375 sec ∴ Speed of B : = $$\frac{800}{375}$$ m/sec = $$\left( {\frac{{800}}{{375}} \times \frac{{18}}{5}} \right)$$ km/hr = $$\frac{192}{25}$$ km/hr = $$7\frac{17}{25}$$ km/hr

q: In a 1547 m race, Arjun reaches in 78 seconds, while Karan reaches the finish point in 91 seconds. By how much distance does Arjun beat Karan?
s: Karan, 91 sec → 1547 m 1 sec → 17 m 78 sec → 1326 m Arjun, 78 sec → 1547 m Karan is defeated by Arjun by = 1547 - 1326 = 221 m

q: In a linear race of 500 m, A can beat B by 50 m and in a race of 600 m, B can beat C by 60 m. By how many metres will A beat C in a race of 400 m?
An athlete runs 8 times around a circular field of radius 7 m in 3 minutes 40 seconds. His speed (in km/h) is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Time}} = 3\,\min 40\sec \\ & = 3\frac{{40}}{{60}} \\ & = 3\frac{2}{3} \\ & = \frac{{11}}{3}\min \\ & {\text{Circumference of circle}} = 2\pi r \\ & = 2 \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times 7 \\ & = 44{\text{ m}} \\ & {\text{Distance}} = {\text{Speed}} \times {\text{Time}} \\ & {\text{44}} \times {\text{8}} = {\text{Speed}} \times \frac{{11}}{3} \times 60 \\ & {\text{Speed}} = \frac{{32}}{{20}} \\ & {\text{Speed}} = \frac{8}{5}\,{\text{m/s}} \\ & {\text{Speed}} = \frac{8}{5} \times \frac{{18}}{5}\,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & {\text{Speed}} = \frac{{144}}{{25}}\,{\text{km/hr}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A and B run a 5 km race on a round course of 400 m. If their speed are in the ratio 5 : 4, the number of times, the winner passes the other is
s: Ratio of speed of A and B = 5 : 4 When A runs 500 m, B runs 400 m A will pass B every time when the distance between them is 400 m A will cover = $$\frac{{400}}{{\left( {500 - 400} \right)}}$$ = 2000 m to overtake B each time Number of time = $$\frac{{5000}}{{2000}}$$ = 2.5 ≈ 2 times (because .5 time is not possible)

q: A can run 250 m in 25 sec and B in 30 sec. How many metres start can A give to B in a km race so that the race may end in a dead-heat?
s: A → 250 m → 25 second 1000 m → 100 second B → 2500 m → 30 second 1000 m → 120 second B should run 20 ahead, i.e. 30 30 second → 250 20 second → $$\frac{{250 \times 20}}{{30}}$$ = 166.66 = 166.67 m

s: Beenu, 50 sec → 400 m 1 sec → 8 m 44 sec → 44 × 8 Amit,

q: In a 1000 m race, Arjun, Balaji and Charan are running. Arjun beats Balaji by 100 m, and Balaji beats Charan by 100 m. In the next 1000 m race (the speeds are the same as in the previous), Balaji gives Charan a head start of 100 m, and Arjun gives Balaji a head start of 100 m. Find the distance by which the winner is ahead of the person just behind him.
In a linear race of 1000 m, A beats B by 50 m or 5 seconds. What is the difference between the speeds (in m/s) of A and B?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed of B}} = \frac{{50}}{5} = 10{\text{ m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Time same}} \\ & {\text{Then,}} \end{aligned}$$ $${\text{Difference in speed}} = \frac{{200}}{1} - \frac{{10}}{1} = \frac{{10}}{{19}}$$

q: Geeta runs $$\frac{5}{2}$$ times as fast as Babita. In a race, if Geeta gives a lead of 40 m to Babita, find the distance from the starting point where both of them will meet (correct up to two decimal places).
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Babita's speed}} = 1 \\ & {\text{Geeta's speed}} = \frac{5}{2} \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow {\text{Relative speed in same direction}} \\ & = \frac{5}{2} - 1 = \frac{3}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{Time}} = \frac{{40}}{{\frac{3}{2}}} = \frac{{80}}{3} = 26.66 \\ & {\text{Distance travel by Babita}} \\ & = 1 \times 26.66\, - - - - - \,26.66 \\ & {\text{Total distance}} = 40 + 26.66 \\ & = 66.66 \\ & = 66.67 \end{aligned}$$

q: In a race of 800 m, Ram can beat Shyam by 50 m, and in a race of 600 m, Shyam can beat Ghanshyam by 40 m. By how many metres will Ram beat Ghanshyam in a race of 400 m?
In a race, a cyclist covers a distance of 500 m in 625 sec in the first lap. He covers the second lap of the same length in 375 sec. What is the average speed (in m/sec) of the cyclist?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Average speed}} = \frac{{{\text{Total distance}}}}{{{\text{Total time}}}} \\ & = \frac{{500 + 500}}{{625 + 375}} \\ & = \frac{{1000}}{{1000}} \\ & = 1{\text{ m/s}} \end{aligned}$$

q: In a 1500 m race, if vehicle P gives vehicle Q a start of 200 m, then vehicle P wins the race by 8 sec. Alternatively, if vehicle P gives vehicle Q a start of 400 m, the race ends in a dead heat. How long does vehicle P take to run 1500 m?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{1300}}{{\text{Q}}} - \frac{{1500}}{{\text{P}}} = 8{\text{ }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}\left( {\text{i}} \right) \\ & {\text{and, }}\frac{{1100}}{{\text{Q}}} = \frac{{1500}}{{\text{P}}}{\text{ }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}\left( {{\text{ii}}} \right) \\ & \frac{{\text{P}}}{{\text{Q}}} = \frac{{15}}{{11}} = \frac{{15x}}{{11x}} \\ & {\text{From equation }}\left( {\text{i}} \right) \\ & \frac{{1300}}{{11x}} - \frac{{1500}}{{15x}} = 8 \\ & 19500 - 16500 = 8 \times 11x \times 15x \\ & 3000 = 8 \times 11 \times 15x \\ & x = \frac{{25}}{{11}} \\ & {\text{Time of P to travel 1500m}} = \frac{{1500}}{{15x}} \\ & = \frac{{1500 \times 11}}{{15 \times 25}} \\ & = 44\sec \\ & \\ & {\bf{Alternate}}\,{\bf{solution:}} \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & 11\mu \to 25 \\ & 1\mu \to \frac{{25}}{{11}} \\ & 15\mu \to \frac{{15 \times 25}}{{11}} \\ & {\text{Speed of Q}} = \frac{{200}}{8} = 25 \\ & {\text{Time of P}} = \frac{{1500 \times 11}}{{15 \times 25}} = 44\sec \end{aligned}$$

q: In a 100 m race, A beats B by 20 m and B beats C by 20 m. By how much distance does A beat C.
s: $${\text{A beat C by}} = \frac{{100}}{{25}} \times 9 = 36\,{\text{m}}$$

q: In a 1200 m race, bike A beats bike B by 100 m. Bike B beats bike C by 100 m in a 600 m race. If bike A beats bike C by 30 sec in a 720 m race, then what is the speed of bike C?

q: In a kilometre race, A beats B by 30 seconds and B beats C by 15 seconds. If A beats C by 180 metres, the time taken by A to run 1 kilometre is.
s: Let the time taken by A to cover 1 km = $$x$$ seconds Time taken by B and C = $$x$$ + 30 seconds and $$x$$ + 45 seconds $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{x}{{x + 45}} = \frac{{41}}{{50}} \\ & 50x = 41x + 1845 \\ & x = 205{\text{ seconds}} \end{aligned}$$

q: In a 400 metre race, A runs at a speed of 16 m/sec. If A gives B a start of 15 metres and still beats him by 10 sec, then what is the speed of B?
s: \[\begin{array}{cccccccccccc} {}&{\text{A}}&{\text{B}} \\ {{\text{Distance}} \to }&{400}&{385} \end{array}\] $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{400}}{{\text{A}}} = \frac{{385}}{{\text{B}}} - 10 \\ & \frac{{400}}{{16}} = \frac{{385}}{{\text{B}}} - 10 \\ & 25 + 10 = \frac{{385}}{{\text{B}}} \\ & {\text{B}} = 11 \\ & {\text{Speed of B}} = 11{\text{ m/s}} \end{aligned}$$

q: In a race of 1200 m, Ram can beat Shyam by 200 m or by 20 sec. What must be the speed of Ram?
s: Shyam's speed = $$\frac{{200}}{{20}}$$ = 100 m/sec. Time constant \[\begin{array}{cccccccccccc} {}&{{\text{Ram}}}&{}&{{\text{Shyam}}} \\ {{\text{Distance}} \to }&{1200}&:&{1000} \\ {}&{12}&:&{10} \\ {{\text{Speed}} \to }&{12}&:&{10 = 12} \end{array}\]

q: A can give 40 metres start to B and 70 metres to C in a race of one kilometre how many metres start can B give to C in a race of one kilometre?
s: \[\begin{array}{cccccccccccc} {\text{A}}&{\text{B}}&{\text{C}} \\ {1000}&{960}&{930} \end{array}\] ⇒ B can give C a start of 30 meters in a 960 meters race $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 960\,{\text{units}} \to 30 \\ & 1\,{\text{unit}} \to \frac{1}{{32}} \\ & 1000\,{\text{units}} \to \frac{{1000}}{{32}} = 31\frac{1}{4}{\text{ meters}} \end{aligned}$$

q: In a 1500 m race, Anil beats Bakul by 150 m and in the same race Bakul beats Charles by 75 m. By what distance does Anil beat Charles?
s: \[\begin{array}{cccccccccccc} {}&{{\text{Anil}}}&{}&{{\text{Bakul}}} \\ {{\text{Distance}} \to }&{1500}&{}&{1350} \\ {}&{10}&:&9 \\ {}&{{\text{Bakul}}}&{}&{{\text{Charles}}} \\ {{\text{Distance}} \to }&{1500}&{}&{1425} \\ {}&{60}&:&{57} \end{array}\] Anil beats Charles by $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{87}}{{600}} \times 1500 \\ & = \frac{{435}}{2} \\ & = 217.50{\text{ m}} \end{aligned}$$
